title: What does the XRPL RequireAuth account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of RequireAuth and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, RequireAuth makes holders obtain issuer authorization before holding that issuer's trust-line token balances. [1]

The AccountSet reference restricts enabling it when the issuer already has trust lines. Authorizing a line is a ledger permission, not proof that a legal KYC process was adequate. Inspect the appropriate line-side authorization and issuer identity. A generic trust line or accepted identity credential does not automatically authorize holding every token issued by the same business. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for RequireAuth and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why RequireAuth is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
